title: GKD-Recruiter: Jointly Modeling Social and Task Heterogeneity for Spatial Crowdsourcing via Graph Knowledge Distillation
claim: Real-world referral mechanisms feed a platform where social influence and task-specific affinity jointly determine who is recruited.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, app screenshot feeding a system diagram
description: The figure has two rounded panels. On the left is a Meituan 'Invite Friend, Get Coupon' app screenshot. A blue user icon invites three lighter user icons, above a red and orange coupon card reading ¥20 with an 'Invite Now' button. It is labeled 'Social Invitation Mechanism'. A blue arrow leads right to the main panel. That panel shows a city map with worker icons, task pins and trajectory lines. Data and Perform Task arrows connect the map to an orange Spatial Crowdsourcing Platform box, which holds Proper Tasks, Active Workers and a Select arrow. Below it, a light-blue box contains Influence probability calculation, Worker Pool and Task Diffusion modules. Under those is a social network graph of blue and orange user nodes. Arrows labeled Effective Task Satisfaction, Task Affinity, Candidate Workers and Seed Worker-Task Pairs link the layers.
caption: Motivation: (Left) Social recruitment mechanisms in realworld SC apps (e.g., referral bonuses, social sharing). (Right) Our modeling captures both social influence and task-specific affinity.
abstract: Social recruitment offers a solution to worker scarcity in Spatial Crowdsourcing (SC) but faces challenges that are often ignored in traditional Influence Maximization. First, task heterogeneity arising from offline execution constraints breaks the interest-implies-participation assumption, as social influence often fails to translate into physical presence. Second, finite task demand creates a saturation trap, a non-submodular setting in which utility drops sharply to zero once demand is met. To bridge these gaps, we propose GKD-Recruiter, a Task-Aware framework designed to maximize Effective Task Satisfaction (ETS). We explicitly model the complex worker-task affinity via a heterogeneous graph and capture directional social influence using a novel Influential GAT. To robustly fuse these distinct signals, we introduce a Graph Knowledge Distillation mechanism. Furthermore, we employ Rainbow DQN to navigate the non-submodular combinatorial search space, avoiding the local optima that trap greedy heuristics. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that GKD-Recruiter significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both solution quality and inference efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/GaoYucen/GKD-Recruiter.
